_comment: Phase 3 depth and light. Level id -> which backdrop world it uses, how much air is in front of that backdrop, how far each tile layer is knocked back, and where the lights are. levels/*.json is geometry only and did not change for this phase; this is the mood, kept apart from it so an artist can re-light the game without touching a single tile.

_fields.air: haze quad drawn over the parallax and behind the tiles: ramp step + alpha
_fields.bg_tint: multiplier on the background tile layer: ramp step for the hue, mix for how much of that hue, scale for how far back it sits
_fields.fg_tint: the same for the solid layer. Keep it near 1.0 - this is what the player reads as ground
_fields.vignette: 0..1 strength of the screen-edge darkening, drawn over the tiles and under the entities
_fields.lights: additive pools at tile coordinates. radius in px, intensity 0..1, flicker 0..1
_fields.emissive: tile id -> a pool on every one of those tiles, merged along a row

_colours: Every ramp/step pair indexes assets/palette.json, which tools/art/palette.py generates. No RGB literals: an ambient tint multiplies the whole screen, so it has to come off the same ramps as the art.

jungle_1._note: CANOPY TRAIL. Daylight. The backdrop does the work; the air is only thick enough to keep the far trees behind the tiles.

jungle_2._note: ROOT HOLLOW. The dark one. Its bg layer is a solid wall of bg_rock on every screen, so the parallax is never visible here - all of the depth is tint, vignette and the lights that pick out the route.

jungle_3._note: THE WATERWAY. Also walled in bg_rock, so again no parallax. The water surface lights itself: every run of water_top gets one pool.

jungle_4._note: SKY BRANCH. The bright one. The haze is pale rather than dark, which is the whole trick: it lifts the backdrop towards the sky instead of pushing it towards black.

jungle_5._note: HEART OF THE GROVE. The boss arena: same jungle backdrop as CANOPY TRAIL, pushed violet so the last level does not look like the first one.

test_arena._note: Left neutral on purpose. tools/itest.sh plays here, and a test that has to be re-baselined every time someone re-lights a level is a test nobody trusts.
